en.name: John II
en.summary: The first pope to adopt a new papal name upon election, having been born with the name Mercurius.
en.body: John II began the enduring custom of popes taking a new name upon election, since his birth name, Mercurius, honored a pagan god and was considered unsuitable for a bishop of Rome. His reign saw the emperor Justinian formally acknowledge Roman primacy in a letter addressed to him, even as Justinian's own authority over Italy remained contested amid ongoing Gothic rule.
